title: Joshua 10 — Great stones from the skies and the sun standing still at Giv'on (Gibeon)

translation.sourceText: Hebrew Masoretic text (Westminster Leningrad Codex base, Public Domain) — Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra

verdicts.reasoning: wayyaḥărîmāh 'had devoted it to destruction' (ḥērem convention); the parenthetical comparison is kept with dashes. Exact.
wayyîrʾû məʾōḏ ... kəʾaḥaṯ ʿārê hammamlāḵâ: plural subject (Adoni-Tzedeq's people) kept as 'they'. Exact.
Names re-checked against the MT: hôhām, pirʾām, yāp̄îaʿ, dəḇîr; Hevron, Yarmut, Lakhish, Eglon. Transliteration per overlay.
ʿălû-ʾēlay wəʿizrunî wənakkeh ʾeṯ-giḇʿôn kî-hišlîmâ: exact.
ḥămēšeṯ malḵê hāʾĕmōrî ... wayyillāḥămû ʿāleyhā: exact; 'Emorites' under the '-ite' rule.
ʾal-terep̄ yāḏêḵā mēʿăḇāḏêḵā 'Do not let your hands go slack from your servants'; yōšəḇê hāhār 'who dwell in the hill country'. Exact.
wayyaʿal ... hûʾ wəḵol-ʿam hammilḥāmâ ʿimmô wəḵōl gibbôrê heḥāyil: exact.
ʾal-tîrāʾ mēhem kî ḇəyāḏəḵā nəṯattîm lōʾ-yaʿămōḏ ʾîš mēhem bəp̄ānêḵā: exact.
wayyāḇōʾ ... pitʾōm kol-hallaylâ ʿālâ: 'all the night he had gone up' (pluperfect). Exact.

citations: Boling and Wright, Joshua (AB 6; 1982), ad loc.
verdicts.reasoning: wayhummēm YHWH ... wayyakkēm ... wayyirdəp̄ēm ... wayyakkēm: the MT keeps YHWH as grammatical subject and the line keeps 'he'; the plural of some Greek witnesses and the commentators' alternatives are recorded. Defensible under the MT-baseline rule.

Re-parsed: wayhwh hišlîḵ ʿălêhem ʾăḇānîm gəḏōlôṯ min-haššāmayim ... ʾaḇnê habbārāḏ. Both nouns literal, so the narrator's identification of the stones as hail is visible; 'from the skies' follows the ratified register clause (weather; cf. 2 Kgs 1:10-14). The reception note accurately reports TBWTT ch. 3 ('bombardment') and is kept out of the line.

citations: Holladay, "The Day(s) the Moon Stood Still", JBL 87 (1968)
verdicts.reasoning: šemeš bəḡiḇʿôn dôm wəyārēaḥ bəʿēmeq ʾayyālôn: 'stand still' (ASV) is supported by ʿāmaḏ in v 13; the alternatives (cessation of light, omen reading) are set out without being chosen. tēṯ YHWH ʾeṯ-hāʾĕmōrî lip̄nê 'gave up the Emorites before'. Defensible.

wayyiddōm haššemeš wəyārēaḥ ʿāmāḏ ʿaḏ-yiqqōm gôy ʾōyəḇāyw ... baḥăṣî haššāmayim ... kəyôm tāmîm: literal; 'Book of Yashar' transliterated as a title; LXX absence of the citation and LXX 1 Kgs 8:53a 'book of the song' accurately reported. Reception note confined to apparatus.
wəlōʾ hāyâ kayyôm hahûʾ ... lišmōaʿ YHWH bəqôl ʾîš kî YHWH nilḥām ləyiśrāʾēl: exact.
MT verse (absent from the LXX, as is v 43) translated, with the narrative tension with v 21 stated. Correct under the MT-baseline rule.
wayyānusû ... wayyēḥāḇəʾû bamməʿārâ bəmaqqēḏâ: exact.
nimṣəʾû ḥămēšeṯ hamməlāḵîm neḥbəʾîm bamməʿārâ: exact.
gōllû ʾăḇānîm gəḏōlôṯ ʾel-pî hamməʿārâ wəhap̄qîḏû ʿāleyhā ʾănāšîm ləšomrām: exact.
wəzinnaḇtem ʾôṯām 'strike their rear' (denominative of zānāḇ); YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem 'YHWH your Elohim' under clause 3. Exact.
ʿaḏ-tummām wəhaśśərîḏîm śārəḏû mēhem: 'the survivors who survived of them' keeps the cognate construction. Exact.
lōʾ-ḥāraṣ liḇnê yiśrāʾēl ləʾîš ʾeṯ-ləšōnô: 'no one moved his tongue against any of the children of Yisra'el' (cf. Ex 11:7). Exact.
pitḥû ʾeṯ-pî hamməʿārâ wəhôṣîʾû ʾēlay: exact.
Five kings listed in MT order. Exact.
hehāləḵûʾ with anomalous final aleph (also Isa 28:12) is correctly analysed and translated as the ordinary verb; qəṣînê 'chiefs'. Exact.
ʾal-tîrʾû wəʾal-tēḥāttû ḥizqû wəʾimṣû: exact.
wayyakkēm ... wayəmîṯēm wayyiṯlēm ʿal ḥămiššâ ʿēṣîm: execution then exposure, as the note says (Deut 21:22-23). Exact.
ləʿēṯ bôʾ haššemeš ... ʿaḏ-ʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh 'unto this very day'. Exact.
heḥĕrîm ʾôṯām wəʾeṯ-kol-hannep̄eš: 'he devoted them to destruction, and every person' (MT plural ʾôṯām; many MSS ʾôṯāh, not adopted, acceptable). nepeš 'person' per the nefesh entry. Exact.
wayyaʿăḇōr ... mimmaqqēḏâ liḇnâ wayyillāḥem ʿim-liḇnâ: exact.
wayyittēn YHWH gam-ʾôṯāh ... lōʾ-hišʾîr bāh śārîḏ: exact.
lāḵîšâ wayyiḥan ʿāleyhā wayyillāḥem bāh: exact.
wayyilkəḏāh bayyôm haššēnî: exact.
ʾāz ʿālâ hōrām meleḵ gezer ... ʿaḏ-biltî hišʾîr-lô śārîḏ: exact.
millāḵîš ʿeḡlōnâ wayyaḥănû ... wayyillāḥămû: plural verbs kept. Exact.
bayyôm hahûʾ heḥĕrîm 'he devoted to destruction on that day' (ḥērem convention). Exact.
wayyaʿal ... mēʿeḡlônâ ḥeḇrônâ: exact.
wəʾeṯ-malkāh: the note correctly flags that Hevron's king died at v 26. wayyaḥărēm 'devoted it to destruction'; kol-hannep̄eš twice. Exact.
wayyāšāḇ ... dəḇirâ: 'returned' (šûḇ, a turn of direction). Exact.
wayyaḥărîmû ʾeṯ-kol-nep̄eš: exact under the ḥērem and nefesh entries.
hāhār wəhanneḡeḇ wəhaššəp̄ēlâ wəhāʾăšēḏôṯ ... kol-hannəšāmâ heḥĕrîm: 'all that breathed'; 'the Negev' for the region is justified. Exact.
miqqāḏēš barnēaʿ wəʿaḏ-ʿazzâ ... ʾereṣ gōšen: exact; Goshen identified as the Judahite district in the note.
lāḵaḏ yəhôšuaʿ paʿam ʾeḥāṯ: 'at one time'. Exact.
Identical to v 15; absent from the LXX; translated. Correct.

Ratify the exception exactly as narrowly worded (MT grammatically impossible + Hebrew-manuscript reading supported by the versions).
founderDecisionRecommendations.2-gentilics: Keep the Kings '-ite' rule in the Former Prophets now (option c); it maps one-to-one to the ASV and is already ratified for Kings. For the later corpus pass, the reviewer prefers (a) '-ite' throughout, with the central pelishtim-caphtor plural becoming 'the Pelishtites', because 'the Pelishtite' beside 'the Pelishtim' is the one jarring pair. No philological issue either way; it is a presentation choice.

The ratified Kings text explicitly leaves the central narrative-subject rule ('the Elohim') in force and limits the article-less form to predicates, genitives and direct-speech subjects; the brief's paraphrase was inaccurate. founderDecisionRecommendations.4-Judg-6:34-clothed: Ship. lāḇəšâ is literally 'clothed' (BDB; same idiom 1 Chr 12:19; 2 Chr 24:20; Block), and keeping Judges' four verbs distinct is a gain in accuracy.
founderDecisionRecommendations.5-herem: Ship. 'devote(d) to destruction' is the standard modern rendering (NRSV; HALOT) and the only consistent one; it makes the Josh 6 / Josh 10 connection visible without moral editorializing.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ כִשְׁמֹ֨עַ אֲדֹֽנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם כִּֽי־לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־הָעַי֮ וַיַּחֲרִימָהּ֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֤ה לִֽירִיחוֹ֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כֵּן־עָשָׂ֥ה לָעַ֖י וּלְמַלְכָּ֑הּ וְכִ֨י הִשְׁלִ֜ימוּ יֹשְׁבֵ֤י גִבְעוֹן֙ אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ בְּקִרְבָּֽם׃

i18n.en: Now it came to pass, when Adoni-Tzedeq king of Yerushalayim heard that Yehoshua had taken Ai and had devoted it to destruction — as he had done to Yericho and its king, so he had done to Ai and its king — and that the inhabitants of Giv'on had made peace with Yisra'el and were among them,

notes.official: Adoni-Tzedeq = Adoni-zedek ('my lord is righteous'; cf. Malki-Tzedeq, Gen 14:18); Yerushalayim = Jerusalem; Giv'on = Gibeon; Yericho = Jericho; Yisra'el = Israel. *heḥĕrîmāh* 'had devoted it to destruction' (ASV 'utterly destroyed'; `herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`). The treaty with Giv'on is narrated in ch. 9.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּֽירְא֣וּ מְאֹ֔ד כִּ֣י עִ֤יר גְּדוֹלָה֙ גִּבְע֔וֹן כְּאַחַ֖ת עָרֵ֣י הַמַּמְלָכָ֑ה וְכִ֨י הִ֤יא גְדוֹלָה֙ מִן־הָעַ֔י וְכָל־אֲנָשֶׁ֖יהָ גִּבֹּרִֽים׃

i18n.en: that they feared greatly, because Giv'on was a great city, like one of the royal cities, and because it was greater than Ai, and all its men were mighty.

notes.official: *kəʾaḥaṯ ʿārê hammamlāḵâ* 'like one of the royal cities'.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אֲדֹנִי־צֶ֜דֶק מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶל־הוֹהָ֣ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶ֠בְרוֹן וְאֶל־פִּרְאָ֨ם מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמ֜וּת וְאֶל־יָפִ֧יעַ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֛ישׁ וְאֶל־דְּבִ֥יר מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֖וֹן לֵאמֹֽר׃

i18n.en: So Adoni-Tzedeq king of Yerushalayim sent to Hoham king of Hevron, and to Pir'am king of Yarmut, and to Yafia king of Lakhish, and to Devir king of Eglon, saying,

notes.official: Hoham king of Hevron (Hebron); Pir'am (Piram) of Yarmut (Jarmuth); Yafia (Japhia) of Lakhish (Lachish); Devir (Debir) of Eglon (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: עֲלֽוּ־אֵלַ֣י וְעִזְרֻ֔נִי וְנַכֶּ֖ה אֶת־גִּבְע֑וֹן כִּֽי־הִשְׁלִ֥ימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: "Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Giv'on; for it has made peace with Yehoshua and with the children of Yisra'el."

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּאָסְפ֨וּ וַֽיַּעֲל֜וּ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת ׀ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֗י מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם מֶֽלֶךְ־חֶבְר֤וֹן מֶֽלֶךְ־יַרְמוּת֙ מֶֽלֶךְ־לָכִ֣ישׁ מֶֽלֶךְ־עֶגְל֔וֹן הֵ֖ם וְכָל־מַֽחֲנֵיהֶ֑ם וַֽיַּחֲנוּ֙ עַל־גִּבְע֔וֹן וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: Therefore the five kings of the Emorites, the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Hevron, the king of Yarmut, the king of Lakhish, the king of Eglon, gathered themselves together and went up, they and all their armies, and encamped against Giv'on and made war against it.

notes.official: *ḥămēšeṯ malḵê hāʾĕmōrî* 'the five kings of the Emorites': here 'Emorite' covers the hill-country population of the south in general (cf. Gen 15:16; Deut 1:7) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלְח֣וּ אַנְשֵׁי֩ גִבְע֨וֹן אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶה֙ הַגִּלְגָּ֣לָה לֵאמֹ֔ר אַל־תֶּ֥רֶף יָדֶ֖יךָ מֵֽעֲבָדֶ֑יךָ עֲלֵ֧ה אֵלֵ֣ינוּ מְהֵרָ֗ה וְהוֹשִׁ֤יעָה לָּ֙נוּ֙ וְעָזְרֵ֔נוּ כִּ֚י נִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֵלֵ֔ינוּ כָּל־מַלְכֵ֥י הָאֱמֹרִ֖י יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָהָֽר׃

i18n.en: And the men of Giv'on sent to Yehoshua, to the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not let your hands go slack from your servants; come up to us quickly, and save us, and help us; for all the kings of the Emorites who dwell in the hill country have gathered against us."

notes.official: *ʾal-terep̄ yāḏêḵā mēʿăḇāḏêḵā* 'Do not let your hands go slack from your servants'. Gilgal.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַל יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ מִן־הַגִּלְגָּ֗ל ה֚וּא וְכָל־עַ֤ם הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וְכֹ֖ל גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י הֶחָֽיִל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So Yehoshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty men of valor.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א מֵהֶ֔ם כִּ֥י בְיָדְךָ֖ נְתַתִּ֑ים לֹֽא־יַעֲמֹ֥ד אִ֛ישׁ מֵהֶ֖ם בְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: And YHWH said to Yehoshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand; not a man of them shall stand before you."

notes.official: *ʾal-tîrāʾ mēhem* 'Do not fear them' (`al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`); *kî ḇəyāḏəḵā nəṯattîm* 'for I have given them into your hand' (`be-yedkhem-nittanu`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֲלֵיהֶ֛ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פִּתְאֹ֑ם כָּל־הַלַּ֕יְלָה עָלָ֖ה מִן־הַגִּלְגָּֽל׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua came upon them suddenly; all the night he had gone up from Gilgal.

notes.official: *pitʾōm* 'suddenly', after an all-night march up from Gilgal.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהֻמֵּ֤ם יְהוָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּכֵּ֥ם מַכָּֽה־גְדוֹלָ֖ה בְּגִבְע֑וֹן וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֗ם דֶּ֚רֶךְ מַעֲלֵ֣ה בֵית־חוֹרֹ֔ן וַיַּכֵּ֥ם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וְעַד־מַקֵּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And YHWH threw them into panic before Yisra'el, and he struck them with a great slaughter at Giv'on, and pursued them by the way of the ascent of Beit-Choron, and struck them as far as Azeqah and Maqqedah.

notes.official: *wayhummēm YHWH* 'And YHWH threw them into panic' (ASV 'discomfited'): *hmm* is the verb of divine panic in the holy-war narratives (Ex 14:24; 23:27; Judg 4:15; 1 Sam 7:10). In the MT the following verbs, *wayyakkēm ... wayyirdəp̄ēm ... wayyakkēm* 'and he struck them ... pursued them ... struck them', keep YHWH as grammatical subject. Many commentators take Yisra'el or Yehoshua as the subject, and some Greek witnesses have plurals; the line keeps the singular 'he' (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Beit-Choron = Beth-horon; Azeqah = Azekah; Maqqedah = Makkedah.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֞י בְּנֻסָ֣ם ׀ מִפְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֵ֞ם בְּמוֹרַ֤ד בֵּית־חוֹרֹן֙ וַֽיהוָ֡ה הִשְׁלִ֣יךְ עֲלֵיהֶם֩ אֲבָנִ֨ים גְּדֹל֧וֹת מִן־הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם עַד־עֲזֵקָ֖ה וַיָּמֻ֑תוּ רַבִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁר־מֵ֙תוּ֙ בְּאַבְנֵ֣י הַבָּרָ֔ד מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָרְג֛וּ בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בֶּחָֽרֶב׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And it came to pass, as they fled from before Yisra'el, while they were on the descent of Beit-Choron, that YHWH threw down on them great stones from the skies, as far as Azeqah, and they died; there were more who died by the hailstones than those whom the children of Yisra'el killed with the sword.

notes.official:
*YHWH hišlîḵ ʿălêhem ʾăḇānîm gəḏōlôṯ min-haššāmayim ... ʾaḇnê habbārāḏ* 'YHWH threw down on them great stones from the skies ... the hailstones': the narrator first calls them 'great stones' and then, in the same sentence, identifies them as hail (`avne-barad-great-stones-hailstones-joshua-10-11`). *min-haššāmayim* 'from the skies' (ASV 'from heaven') follows the register rule of central `shamayim`, which keeps 'skies' for weather and the physical sky. Hail as YHWH's weapon recurs at Ex 9:18-26, Job 38:22-23 (central `otzrot-sheleg-barad`), Isa 30:30 and Ezek 38:22.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) quotes this verse ('Yahweh cast down great stones from heaven upon them') and reads it as an aerial bombardment that killed more than the Israelites' swords. The line renders the nouns literally, including the narrator's identification of the stones as hail, and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: אָ֣ז יְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה בְּי֗וֹם תֵּ֤ת יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י לִפְנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ לְעֵינֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שֶׁ֚מֶשׁ בְּגִבְע֣וֹן דּ֔וֹם וְיָרֵ֖חַ בְּעֵ֥מֶק אַיָּלֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: Then Yehoshua spoke to YHWH on the day when YHWH gave up the Emorites before the children of Yisra'el, and he said in the sight of Yisra'el, "Sun, stand still at Giv'on, and moon, in the valley of Ayyalon."

notes.official: *šemeš bəḡiḇʿôn dôm wəyārēaḥ bəʿēmeq ʾayyālôn* 'Sun, stand still at Giv'on, and moon, in the valley of Ayyalon' (Ayyalon = Aijalon): a poetic couplet, here printed as prose, which v 13 cites from the Book of Yashar. *dôm* (from *dmm*) means 'be still, be silent, wait' (BDB; HALOT); the ASV 'stand still' is kept, and v 13 takes it up with *wayyiddōm* and *ʿāmāḏ* 'stood' (`shemesh-dom-sun-stand-still-joshua-10-12-13`). The request has been read as a halt of the sun, as a cessation of its light or heat (darkening, eclipse or cloud), and, by comparison with Mesopotamian omen texts, as a prayer for a favourable position of sun and moon (Holladay, 'The Day(s) the Moon Stood Still', JBL 87, 1968; Walton, 'Joshua 10:12-15 and Mesopotamian Celestial Omen Texts', 1994). The line does not decide between these readings. In the MT Yehoshua speaks 'to YHWH' and then addresses sun and moon 'in the sight of Yisra'el'. 'the Emorites' (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּדֹּ֨ם הַשֶּׁ֜מֶשׁ וְיָרֵ֣חַ עָמָ֗ד עַד־יִקֹּ֥ם גּוֹי֙ אֹֽיְבָ֔יו הֲלֹא־הִ֥יא כְתוּבָ֖ה עַל־סֵ֣פֶר הַיָּשָׁ֑ר וַיַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַשֶּׁ֙מֶשׁ֙ בַּחֲצִ֣י הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וְלֹא־אָ֥ץ לָב֖וֹא כְּי֥וֹם תָּמִֽים׃

i18n.en: And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged itself on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Yashar? And the sun stayed in the midst of the skies and did not hasten to go down for about a whole day.

notes.official:
*wayyiddōm haššemeš wəyārēaḥ ʿāmāḏ ʿaḏ-yiqqōm gôy ʾōyəḇāyw* 'And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged itself on its enemies' (`shemesh-dom-sun-stand-still-joshua-10-12-13`). *sēp̄er hayyāšār* 'the Book of Yashar' (ASV 'Jashar'): a lost book of poetry, also cited at 2 Sam 1:18; *yāšār* means 'upright' (`sefer-hayyashar-book-of-yashar-joshua-10-13`). The LXX lacks the reference here (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). The LXX of 1 Kgs 8:53a cites a 'book of the song' (*šîr*), which many take as a metathesis of *yšr* (Nelson, *Joshua*). The later works called 'the Book of Jasher' (a medieval Hebrew midrash; an eighteenth-century English forgery) are unrelated. *baḥăṣî haššāmayim* 'in the midst of the skies' (physical sky, central `shamayim`); *kəyôm tāmîm* 'about a whole day'.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) reads 'about a whole day' as the duration of a lightning war, so short for the territory taken that people believed the sun had stopped. The line renders *dmm*, *ʿmd* and *kəyôm tāmîm* literally and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹ֨א הָיָ֜ה כַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לְפָנָ֣יו וְאַחֲרָ֔יו לִשְׁמֹ֥עַ יְהוָ֖ה בְּק֣וֹל אִ֑ישׁ כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה נִלְחָ֖ם לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And there was no day like that before it or after it, that YHWH listened to the voice of a man; for YHWH fought for Yisra'el.

notes.official: *lišmōaʿ YHWH bəqôl ʾîš* 'that YHWH listened to the voice of a man'; *kî YHWH nilḥām ləyiśrāʾēl* 'for YHWH fought for Yisra'el' (`yhwh-yilachem-lakhem-divine-warrior-formula-ex-14-13-14-cross-corpus`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּֽלָה׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra'el with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

notes.official: Absent from the LXX, as is the identical v 43. In the MT it anticipates the end of the campaign before vv 16-42, where the people are still at Maqqedah (v 21). The MT is translated in full (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּנֻ֕סוּ חֲמֵ֖שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיֵּחָבְא֥וּ בַמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And these five kings fled and hid themselves in the cave at Maqqedah.

paragraphs.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לִיהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ לֵאמֹ֑ר נִמְצְאוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֔ים נֶחְבְּאִ֥ים בַּמְּעָרָ֖ה בְּמַקֵּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: And it was told Yehoshua, saying, "The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Maqqedah."

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ גֹּ֛לּוּ אֲבָנִ֥ים גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֶל־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהַפְקִ֧ידוּ עָלֶ֛יהָ אֲנָשִׁ֖ים לְשָׁמְרָֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua said, "Roll great stones to the mouth of the cave, and set men by it to guard them.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתֶּם֙ אַֽל־תַּעֲמֹ֔דוּ רִדְפוּ֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אֹֽיְבֵיכֶ֔ם וְזִנַּבְתֶּ֖ם אוֹתָ֑ם אַֽל־תִּתְּנ֗וּם לָבוֹא֙ אֶל־עָ֣רֵיהֶ֔ם כִּ֧י נְתָנָ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיֶדְכֶֽם׃

i18n.en: But as for you, do not stay; pursue your enemies and strike their rear; do not let them enter their cities, for YHWH your Elohim has given them into your hand."

notes.official: *YHWH ʾĕlōhêḵem* 'YHWH your Elohim' (clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִי֩ כְּכַלּ֨וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל לְהַכּוֹתָ֛ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה־מְאֹ֖ד עַד־תֻּמָּ֑ם וְהַשְּׂרִידִים֙ שָׂרְד֣וּ מֵהֶ֔ם וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ אֶל־עָרֵ֥י הַמִּבְצָֽר׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when Yehoshua and the children of Yisra'el had finished striking them with a very great slaughter, until they were consumed, and the survivors who survived of them had entered the fortified cities,

paragraphs.text: וַיָּשֻׁבוּ֩ כָל־הָעָ֨ם אֶל־הַמַּחֲנֶ֧ה אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מַקֵּדָ֖ה בְּשָׁל֑וֹם לֹֽא־חָרַ֞ץ לִבְנֵ֧י יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל לְאִ֖ישׁ אֶת־לְשֹׁנֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: that all the people returned to the camp, to Yehoshua at Maqqedah, in peace; no one moved his tongue against any of the children of Yisra'el.

notes.official: *lōʾ-ḥāraṣ ... ləʾîš ʾeṯ-ləšōnô* 'no one moved his tongue against' (cf. Ex 11:7): no one dared threaten Israel.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ פִּתְח֖וּ אֶת־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֑ה וְהוֹצִ֣יאוּ אֵלַ֗י אֶת־חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן־הַמְּעָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then Yehoshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave, and bring out to me these five kings from the cave."

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עֲשׂוּ כֵ֔ן וַיֹּצִ֣יאוּ אֵלָ֗יו אֶת־חֲמֵ֛שֶׁת הַמְּלָכִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה מִן־הַמְּעָרָ֑ה אֵ֣ת ׀ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם אֶת־מֶ֤לֶךְ חֶבְרוֹן֙ אֶת־מֶ֣לֶךְ יַרְמ֔וּת אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ לָכִ֖ישׁ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ עֶגְלֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And they did so, and brought out to him these five kings from the cave: the king of Yerushalayim, the king of Hevron, the king of Yarmut, the king of Lakhish, the king of Eglon.

paragraphs.text: וַ֠יְהִי כְּֽהוֹצִיאָ֞ם אֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵלֶּה֮ אֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ֒ וַיִּקְרָ֨א יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ אֶל־כָּל־אִ֣ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַ֠יֹּאמֶר אֶל־קְצִינֵ֞י אַנְשֵׁ֤י הַמִּלְחָמָה֙ הֶהָלְכ֣וּא אִתּ֔וֹ קִרְב֗וּ שִׂ֚ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיכֶ֔ם עַֽל־צַוְּארֵ֖י הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַֽיִּקְרְב֔וּ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶת־רַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־צַוְּארֵיהֶֽם׃

i18n.en: And it came to pass, when they brought out these kings to Yehoshua, that Yehoshua called for all the men of Yisra'el, and said to the chiefs of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near, put your feet on the necks of these kings." And they came near and put their feet on their necks.

notes.official: *hehāləḵûʾ* 'who had gone' is written with an anomalous final aleph, one of a handful of such forms (cf. Isa 28:12; GKC §23i), not marked as Ketiv/Qere in the source edition; it is translated as the ordinary verb (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`). Putting a foot on the neck of a defeated enemy is a gesture of victory attested in Near Eastern iconography (cf. Ps 110:1).

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶם֙ יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ אַל־תִּֽירְא֖וּ וְאַל־תֵּחָ֑תּוּ חִזְק֣וּ וְאִמְצ֔וּ כִּ֣י כָ֗כָה יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְכָל־אֹ֣יְבֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נִלְחָמִ֥ים אוֹתָֽם׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua said to them, "Do not fear, nor be dismayed; be strong and of good courage; for thus YHWH will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."

notes.official: *ʾal-tîrʾû wəʾal-tēḥāttû ḥizqû wəʾimṣû* 'Do not fear, nor be dismayed; be strong and of good courage' (`al-tira-fear-not-divine-encouragement-formula`), the charge of 1:6-9 passed on to the army.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכֵּ֨ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֤עַ אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵן֙ וַיְמִיתֵ֔ם וַיִּתְלֵ֕ם עַ֖ל חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה עֵצִ֑ים וַיִּֽהְי֛וּ תְּלוּיִ֥ם עַל־הָעֵצִ֖ים עַד־הָעָֽרֶב׃

i18n.en: And afterward Yehoshua struck them and put them to death, and hanged them on five trees; and they were hanging on the trees until the evening.

notes.official: *wayyiṯlēm ʿal ḥămiššâ ʿēṣîm* 'and hanged them on five trees': the bodies are exposed after the execution and taken down at sunset (v 27), as Deut 21:22-23 requires.

paragraphs.text: וַיְהִ֞י לְעֵ֣ת ׀ בּ֣וֹא הַשֶּׁ֗מֶשׁ צִוָּ֤ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ וַיֹּֽרִידוּם֙ מֵעַ֣ל הָעֵצִ֔ים וַיַּ֨שְׁלִכֻ֔ם אֶל־הַמְּעָרָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר נֶחְבְּאוּ־שָׁ֑ם וַיָּשִׂ֜מוּ אֲבָנִ֤ים גְּדֹלוֹת֙ עַל־פִּ֣י הַמְּעָרָ֔ה עַד־עֶ֖צֶם הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And it came to pass at the time of the going down of the sun that Yehoshua commanded, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden themselves, and laid great stones on the mouth of the cave, unto this very day.

notes.official: *ʿaḏ-ʿeṣem hayyôm hazzeh* 'unto this very day' (`ad-ha-yom-ha-zeh-aetiological-formula`): the stones at the mouth of the cave as a landmark.

paragraphs.text: וְאֶת־מַקֵּדָה֩ לָכַ֨ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֜עַ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶרֶב֮ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ הֶחֱרִ֣ם אוֹתָ֗ם וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֙פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֙עַשׂ֙ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ מַקֵּדָ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua took Maqqedah on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king; he devoted them to destruction, and every person that was in it; he left no survivor; and he did to the king of Maqqedah as he had done to the king of Yericho.

notes.official: *heḥĕrîm* 'he devoted ... to destruction' (`herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`). *kol-hannep̄eš ʾăšer-bāh* 'every person that was in it' (ASV 'all the souls'): *nepeš* as 'person, living being', rendered idiomatically under `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets` (also vv 30, 32, 35, 37, 39). *lōʾ hišʾîr śārîḏ* 'he left no survivor'. Maqqedah = Makkedah.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִמַּקֵּדָ֖ה לִבְנָ֑ה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עִם־לִבְנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua passed on from Maqqedah, and all Yisra'el with him, to Livnah, and fought against Livnah.

notes.official: Livnah = Libnah.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה גַּם־אוֹתָ֜הּ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל וְאֶת־מַלְכָּהּ֒ וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֗רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֙פֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֥יר בָּ֖הּ שָׂרִ֑יד וַיַּ֣עַשׂ לְמַלְכָּ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה לְמֶ֥לֶךְ יְרִיחֽוֹ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And YHWH gave it also, and its king, into the hand of Yisra'el; and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person that was in it; he left no survivor in it; and he did to its king as he had done to the king of Yericho.

notes.official: *kol-hannep̄eš* 'every person' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִלִּבְנָ֖ה לָכִ֑ישָׁה וַיִּ֣חַן עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua passed on from Livnah, and all Yisra'el with him, to Lakhish, and encamped against it and fought against it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֶת־לָכִ֜ישׁ בְּיַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל וַֽיִּלְכְּדָהּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשֵּׁנִ֔י וַיַּכֶּ֣הָ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֑הּ כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְלִבְנָֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And YHWH gave Lakhish into the hand of Yisra'el, and he took it on the second day, and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person that was in it, according to all that he had done to Livnah.

notes.official: Lakhish = Lachish; *bayyôm haššēnî* 'on the second day'. *kol-hannep̄eš* 'every person' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: אָ֣ז עָלָ֗ה הֹרָם֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ גֶּ֔זֶר לַעְזֹ֖ר אֶת־לָכִ֑ישׁ וַיַּכֵּ֤הוּ יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ וְאֶת־עַמּ֔וֹ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃

i18n.en: Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lakhish; and Yehoshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מִלָּכִ֖ישׁ עֶגְלֹ֑נָה וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ עָלֶ֔יהָ וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua passed on from Lakhish, and all Yisra'el with him, to Eglon; and they encamped against it and fought against it.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּד֜וּהָ בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּהָ לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וְאֵת֙ כָּל־הַנֶּ֣פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא הֶחֱרִ֑ים כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְלָכִֽישׁ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And they took it on that day, and struck it with the edge of the sword; and every person that was in it he devoted to destruction on that day, according to all that he had done to Lakhish.

notes.official: *heḥĕrîm* 'he devoted to destruction' (`herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`); *kol-hannep̄eš* 'every person' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣עַל יְ֠הוֹשֻׁעַ וְכָֽל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֛וֹ מֵעֶגְל֖וֹנָה חֶבְר֑וֹנָה וַיִּֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua went up from Eglon, and all Yisra'el with him, to Hevron; and they fought against it.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּלְכְּד֣וּהָ וַיַּכּֽוּהָ־לְפִי־חֶ֠רֶב וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֨הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־עָרֶ֜יהָ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֤פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּהּ֙ לֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֣יר שָׂרִ֔יד כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֖ה לְעֶגְל֑וֹן וַיַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּֽהּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: And they took it and struck it with the edge of the sword, and its king, and all its cities, and every person that was in it; he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon; and he devoted it to destruction, and every person that was in it.

notes.official: Hevron = Hebron. *wayyaḥărēm ʾôṯāh* 'and he devoted it to destruction' (`herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`); *kol-hannep̄eš* 'every person', twice (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`). Hevron's king was killed at v 26; the reference to 'its king' here may concern a successor or reflect a formula.

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֧שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל עִמּ֖וֹ דְּבִ֑רָה וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם עָלֶֽיהָ׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra'el with him, to Devir, and fought against it.

notes.official: Devir = Debir.

paragraphs.text: וַֽיִּלְכְּדָ֞הּ וְאֶת־מַלְכָּ֤הּ וְאֶת־כָּל־עָרֶ֙יהָ֙ וַיַּכּ֣וּם לְפִי־חֶ֔רֶב וַֽיַּחֲרִ֙ימוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־נֶ֣פֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֔הּ לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר עָשָׂ֜ה לְחֶבְר֗וֹן כֵּן־עָשָׂ֤ה לִדְבִ֙רָה֙ וּלְמַלְכָּ֔הּ וְכַאֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֛ה לְלִבְנָ֖ה וּלְמַלְכָּֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And he took it, and its king, and all its cities; and they struck them with the edge of the sword, and devoted to destruction every person that was in it; he left no survivor; as he had done to Hevron, so he did to Devir and to its king, and as he had done to Livnah and to its king.

notes.official: *wayyaḥărîmû* 'and devoted to destruction' (`herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`); *kol-nep̄eš* 'every person' (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכֶּ֣ה יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ אֶת־כָּל־הָאָ֡רֶץ הָהָר֩ וְהַנֶּ֨גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָ֜ה וְהָאֲשֵׁד֗וֹת וְאֵת֙ כָּל־מַלְכֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א הִשְׁאִ֖יר שָׂרִ֑יד וְאֵ֤ת כָּל־הַנְּשָׁמָה֙ הֶחֱרִ֔ים כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוָּ֔ה יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: So Yehoshua struck all the land, the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the slopes, and all their kings; he left no survivor, and he devoted to destruction all that breathed, as YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, commanded.

notes.official: *hāhār wəhanneḡeḇ wəhaššəp̄ēlâ wəhāʾăšēḏôṯ* 'the hill country and the Negev and the lowland and the slopes': *hanneḡeḇ* is the southern region, 'the Negev' (ASV 'the South') (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`). *kol-hannəšāmâ heḥĕrîm* 'he devoted to destruction all that breathed' (cf. Deut 20:16; `herem-devoted-devote-to-destruction-joshua`). *YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (`elohei-yisrael`; clause 3 of `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּכֵּ֧ם יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ מִקָּדֵ֥שׁ בַּרְנֵ֖עַ וְעַד־עַזָּ֑ה וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־אֶ֥רֶץ גֹּ֖שֶׁן וְעַד־גִּבְעֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And Yehoshua struck them from Qadesh-Barnea as far as Azzah, and all the land of Goshen, as far as Giv'on.

notes.official: Qadesh-Barnea = Kadesh-barnea; Azzah = Gaza (transliterated, since it is not one of the few names Kings keeps in English); Goshen here is a district in the south of Yehudah (cf. 11:16; 15:51), not the Goshen of Egypt (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-former-prophets`).

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־הַמְּלָכִ֤ים הָאֵ֙לֶּה֙ וְאֶת־אַרְצָ֔ם לָכַ֥ד יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ פַּ֣עַם אֶחָ֑ת כִּ֗י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נִלְחָ֖ם לְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: And all these kings and their land Yehoshua took at one time, because YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, fought for Yisra'el.

notes.official: *paʿam ʾeḥāṯ* 'at one time'. *kî YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl nilḥām ləyiśrāʾēl* 'because YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, fought for Yisra'el' (`yhwh-yilachem-lakhem-divine-warrior-formula-ex-14-13-14-cross-corpus`; `elohei-yisrael`).

paragraphs.text: וַיָּ֤שָׁב יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ וְכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עִמּ֔וֹ אֶל־הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה הַגִּלְגָּֽלָה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: And Yehoshua returned, and all Yisra'el with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

notes.official: Absent from the LXX, like v 15 (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-former-prophets`).
